subject: Request: pro-rata SLA assessment for multi-region degradation
messages:
From: Laura Simmons <laura.simmons@acme.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@acme.com
Date: Fri, 4 Sep 2026 11:12:03 -0400
Subject: Re: unusual errors impacting inference endpoints

Hannah / Redwood team,

We saw a jump in 5xxs and tail latency starting ~08:20 PT on Friday that affected our `payments-embed` and `nlp-chat` routes in us-east and us-west. Downstream retries exacerbated the backlog. Our side tracked user impact to roughly 2.5 hours (08:20–10:50 PT) — roughly 18% of traffic for those endpoints failed or timed out.

We opened an internal incident (INC-ACME-993) and are collecting traces; attached are the sample logs. Can Redwood confirm the service-level observed on your side and advise whether this meets the criteria for a pro-rata credit under our contract? We want the credit calculation scoped to the impacted endpoints only, not the entire account.

Thanks,
Laura Simmons
SRE Lead, Acme Corp

Attachments: svc-logs-acme-sample.log (text), request-trace-09-04.json (text)

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Simmons <laura.simmons@acme.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 4 Sep 2026 09:05:11 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: pro-rata SLA assessment for multi-region degradation

Laura — thanks for the heads up and for attaching the logs. We’ve pulled preliminary telemetry for that window. High level: there was an elevated error-rate correlation with a routing flapping event between clusters in us-east and us-west that caused increased queue times for some shards.

Quick answers up-front:
- We can confirm an availability impact that overlaps with your reported window (approx 08:18–10:52 PT).
- We can run a pro-rata credit calculation scoped to the affected model routes. To do that cleanly we need your list of impacted endpoints (route names) and any customer-specific routing overrides.
- We will provide a full postmortem and the raw server-side logs (compressed) for your audit.

Can you confirm the exact routes to scope? Also copying Dev and Marissa from our Escalations + CS teams to coordinate credits and the postmortem timeline.

—Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
Phone: +1-415-555-0193

Attachment: svc-logs-2026-09-04.zip (log archive, 24MB)

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Laura Simmons <laura.simmons@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 4 Sep 2026 10:32:47 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: pro-rata SLA assessment for multi-region degradation

Laura — quick note from engineering: we’re already isolating affected shards and have a preliminary root cause (BG sync between routing controllers triggered a reconfiguration storm). We expect the full technical postmortem ready by EOD Mon (2026-09-07).

For the credit calculation, we propose the following approach (please confirm):
1) Use the per-route availability delta for the exact window 2026-09-04T08:18:00-2026-09-04T10:52:00 PT.
2) Apply pro-rata credit only to billable units for those routes during that window (not to embeddings or unrelated endpoints).
3) Exclude any traffic that was already retried client-side with successful subsequent requests.

We’ve attached our latency summary for the period (latency-summary-09-04.csv) to help cross-validate metrics.

If that methodology looks good, we’ll run the compute and produce a provisional credit number by Monday.

—Dev
Sr. Incident Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment: latency-summary-09-04.csv (CSV)

From: Laura Simmons <laura.simmons@acme.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@acme.com
Date: Fri, 4 Sep 2026 12:07:29 -0400
Subject: Re: Request: pro-rata SLA assessment for multi-region degradation

Thanks, Dev/Hannah. Confirmed impacted routes: `payments-embed`, `nlp-chat`, `invoice-extract`. No routing overrides on our side. We will filter out client retries and provide a short CSV of impacted request IDs by Monday morning.

One ask: please ensure any credit excludes reserved-dedicated capacity that we have under our Dedicated agreement (Section 4.2 of the SLA). The contract language is explicit about dedicated reservation exceptions and we want the credit limited to on-demand usage for the affected API keys.

Appreciate the quick response.

—Laura

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Simmons <laura.simmons@acme.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 7 Sep 2026 16:32:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: pro-rata SLA assessment for multi-region degradation

Hi Laura — thanks for the route list and the CSV of impacted request IDs (received). We ran the scoped calculation per our proposed methodology and here is the provisional result:

- Scoped window: 2026-09-04T08:18:00-2026-09-04T10:52:00 PT
- Affected billable on-demand units (payments-embed, nlp-chat, invoice-extract): 1,142,430 tokens
- Measured availability reduction (weighted by traffic): 6.7% for the scoped routes during the window
- Provisional pro-rata credit: equivalent to 6.7% of on-demand charges for those routes for the billing month, capped at the contractual maximum per Section 3.1(b).

We intentionally excluded Redeemed Reserved (Dedicated) capacity per your note; that showed no net credit impact. Final credit will be issued after we complete the postmortem and validate no overlapping credits have already been applied.

Next steps:
1) We will publish the incident postmortem by EOD Tue (2026-09-08) and include mitigation steps.
2) Finance will generate a credit memo tied to deal ACME-5571 within three business days after the postmortem is accepted.

If anything here looks off, call me directly and we’ll adjust.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
Phone: +1-650-555-0122

Related link: https://hubspot.example.com/deal/5571
Attachments: credit-provision-breakdown.pdf (summary, 120KB)
